title: Finite constant torsors and the etale fundamental group
statement:
Let $U_0/k_0$ be geometrically connected and separated of finite type,
put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and choose a geometric point
$\bar u\to U$. For a finite abelian group $M$, viewed as a constant
etale sheaf on $U$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,M)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\pi_1(U,\bar u),M).
\tag{3.1}
$$

It is natural for automorphisms of the pointed scheme and for the descent
transport attached to a Weil-group element. More precisely, if a lift
$s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ acts on $\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ by conjugation, its
pullback action on the right side of (3.1) is

$$
f\longmapsto\bigl[g\longmapsto f(s^{-1}gs)\bigr].
$$

The Weil-group and etale-cohomology conventions are those of
[def-wf-weil-group], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Put $\Pi=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$; $U$ is connected by geometric connectedness. The natural bijection of [thm-galois-torsor-h1] represents a class $c\in H^1(U,M)$ by an $M$-torsor $P$. Its finite locally constant underlying sheaf is a finite etale cover by [thm-galois-lc-etale]. The torsor conditions of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors] give a nonempty fibre $P_{\bar u}$ and a simply transitive $M$-action: a local section gives a point after choosing a lift of the geometric point to a trivializing etale cover. By [thm-galois-fundamental], $P_{\bar u}$ is a finite continuous $\Pi$-set. Each translation by $m\in M$ is a morphism of covers, so its fibre map commutes with the $\Pi$-action. Choose $p\in P_{\bar u}$ and define $f_P(g)$ uniquely by $g\cdot p=p+f_P(g)$.

source.place: First paragraph, torsor, finite cover and fibre equivalence

proof.text: Commutation gives $(gh)\cdot p=g\cdot(p+f_P(h))=p+f_P(g)+f_P(h)$, so $f_P(gh)=f_P(g)+f_P(h)$. Replacing $p$ by $p+a$ gives $g\cdot(p+a)=p+a+f_P(g)$, using that $M$ is abelian; thus $f_P$ is unchanged. An equivariant torsor isomorphism carries this identity to the other torsor, so $f_P$ depends only on its isomorphism class. The bijection $M\to P_{\bar u}$, $a\mapsto p+a$, identifies $f_P$ with the orbit map $g\mapsto g\cdot p$. This orbit map is continuous by the finite continuous action in [def-galois-fibre-functor], and $M$ has the discrete topology; equivalently its fibres are cosets of the open stabilizer of $p$.

source.place: Second paragraph, homomorphism, continuity and independence

proof.text: Conversely let $f:\Pi\to M$ be a continuous homomorphism and give the finite set $M$ the action $g\cdot a=f(g)+a$. The identity and multiplication laws follow from those of $f$, continuity follows from continuity of $f$, and this action commutes with translations. By [thm-galois-fundamental], the finite $\Pi$-set is the fibre of a finite etale cover; full faithfulness transports the translations and their action identities to the cover. The map $M\times M\to M\times M$, $(m,a)\mapsto(a+m,a)$, is a bijection, and the finite-limit-compatible equivalence reflects this isomorphism. To verify local nonemptiness without assuming the cover is connected, take the preimage of $f$ under the already-existing bijection [cor-galois-abelian-h1]. Its torsor fibre is equivariantly identified with this $M$-set by $a\mapsto p+a$. Full faithfulness identifies its finite etale cover with the one constructed here, and [thm-galois-lc-etale] identifies the underlying sheaves. Thus the constructed cover carries an $M$-torsor in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-torsors], including local nonemptiness. Starting with $P$, the map $a\mapsto p+a$ is both $M$-equivariant and $\Pi$-equivariant, hence recovers $P$ up to isomorphism. Starting with $f$, use $p=0$ to recover $f$. This proves the bijection and is precisely the canonical torsor description of [cor-galois-abelian-h1].

source.place: Third and fourth paragraphs, inverse construction

proof.text: The bijection is an isomorphism of abelian groups. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1], the canonical class of an $M$-torsor is its usual cohomology class, and addition in $H^1(U,M)$ is represented by the contracted product $P\wedge Q=(P\times Q)/M$ for the antidiagonal action $a\cdot(p,q)=(p+a,q-a)$. The equivalence of [thm-galois-fundamental], compatible with finite limits and colimits, identifies its fibre with $(P_{\bar u}\times Q_{\bar u})/M$. If $r=[p,q]$, then $g\cdot r=[p+f_P(g),q+f_Q(g)]=r+f_P(g)+f_Q(g)$, where the residual $M$-action translates either factor. Hence $f_{P\wedge Q}=f_P+f_Q$. The trivial torsor has a fixed fibre point and gives $f=0$. The canonical torsor classification used here is the same as [thm-galois-torsor-h1], whose lifting-torsor construction is the inverse of the canonical class map.

source.place: Fourth paragraph, the isomorphism assertion (additivity made explicit)

proof.text: Let $a:(U,\bar u)\to(U,\bar u)$ be a pointed automorphism. The base-change compatibility of [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies the fibre of $a^*P$ with $P_{\bar u}$, with $g\in\Pi$ acting as $a_*(g)$ on the latter. This identification preserves the translations by $M$. Thus $g\cdot p'=p'+f_P(a_*(g))$ for the point $p'$ corresponding to $p$, so $f_{a^*P}=f_P\circ a_*$. Naturality of [thm-galois-torsor-h1] identifies the class of $a^*P$ with $a^*c$. This is the commutative naturality square for (3.1).

source.place: Fourth paragraph, naturality for pointed automorphisms

proof.text:
Now let $s\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ and $n=\deg(s)$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-etale-weil-transport] to the finite etale cover $P$, using its pullback fibre bijection $\lambda_{s,P}:((\Phi_U^n)^*P)_{\bar u}\to P_{\bar u}$. Its naturality with respect to each translation $t_m:P\to P$ implies $\lambda_{s,P}(x+m)=\lambda_{s,P}(x)+m$. Choose $p'$ mapping to $p$. For every $g\in\Pi$, the asserted intertwining identity gives
$$
\lambda_{s,P}(g\cdot p')=(s^{-1}gs)\cdot p=p+f_P(s^{-1}gs)
=\lambda_{s,P}(p'+f_P(s^{-1}gs)).
$$
Injectivity gives $g\cdot p'=p'+f_P(s^{-1}gs)$, so $f_{(\Phi_U^n)^*P}(g)=f_P(s^{-1}gs)$. By the naturality of [thm-galois-torsor-h1], this torsor represents the pullback of $c$. The pushforward transport $P\to U\xrightarrow{\Phi_U^n}U$ corresponds to conjugation by $s$; its inverse is the pullback in this calculation, which explains the inverse conjugation in the statement.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph, Weil descent with the direction of transport explicit

proof.text: Step 2 already shows independence of the chosen point $p'$. The formula is a continuous homomorphism because it is the monodromy of the pullback torsor; alternatively conjugation by $s$ restricts to a continuous automorphism of $\Pi$. If $s'$ is another lift of the same degree, [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] gives $s'=hs$ for $h\in\Pi$. Since $f_P(h^{-1}gh)=-f_P(h)+f_P(g)+f_P(h)=f_P(g)$, one has $f_P(s'^{-1}gs')=f_P(s^{-1}gs)$. Thus the action is independent of the auxiliary lift. Degree zero gives the identity, and the preceding calculation holds for every integer degree, including inverse powers. Together with Steps 3--5 it proves (3.1) with both stated naturalities.

source.place: Last paragraph, independence and the equivariance conclusion
